subject.title: feat: Let users steer running ACP/sub-agent sessions from Discord (and other chat surfaces)

question: Should the remaining work be owned by the broader steer-mode admission issue, or kept as a Discord ACP/sub-agent thread-specific fix after the shared admission path lands?
rationale: Current main contains a partial runtime fix and an open overlapping PR, but the safe boundary affects shared reply dispatch, Discord ingress, ACP bindings, and cross-thread isolation.

options.title: Use shared admission as canonical
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48003 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 as the canonical path, then verify Discord ACP/sub-agent threads before closing this issue.

options.title: Narrow to Discord ACP threads
options.body: Keep this issue scoped to Discord ACP/sub-agent bound threads and require a focused fix after the shared queue-policy admission layer is settled.

options.title: Defer for broader design
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define a cross-channel active-turn input contract that covers ordinary messages, commands, ACP sessions, and sub-agents together.

recommendation.title: Use shared admission as canonical
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48003 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 as the canonical path, then verify Discord ACP/sub-agent threads before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: They carried the most recent merged steering fix through landing and are the clearest routing point for deciding how to coordinate the remaining admission work.
